descriptions.github:5684431226: Problem When a human files a bug, the hive withholds the closing keyword from the fix PR: validatePRRequestClaims rewrites Closes N to Refs N unless the issue already has hive: reporter-confirmed ( humanFiledBugReason / IsHumanFiledBugReport in src/pkg/github/pr request claims.go , from kubestellar/hive 6781). The fix PR merges and the issue stays open until the reporter confirms the fix with /fixed or the label. That gate makes sense when the reporter saw a symptom and can check whether it went away (the 6500 → 6762/ 6767 case). It works badly for two common kinds of human-filed bugs: 1. Code-sweep findings. A maintainer or contributor reviews a subsystem and files a batch of defects found by reading the code: races, lossy keys, unbounded reads, doc/code drift, tests that don't test the real contract. There's no symptom the reporter observed, so "reporter confirms the symptom is gone"…

descriptions.github:5684207567: What is wrong No handler or middleware limits the request body size. json.NewDecoder(r.Body) reads whatever arrives. With auth on and --bind 0.0.0.0 , an authenticated client can make the server buffer an arbitrarily large body. What we want Add http.MaxBytesReader in the middleware chain that already wraps every route. 1 MiB is far more than any request body the API takes. An oversized body answers 413 as problem+json through respondError . Where to look - src/internal/httpapi/middleware.go and src/internal/httpapi/server.go - src/internal/httpapi/problems.go and docs/adr/0006-api-conventions.md for the error shape - The api-change skill / API docs: any new status code must be listed in the API reference Definition of done - [ ] A body over the limit gets 413 problem+json; a body just under it is accepted. - [ ] The limit applies to every /api/v2 route with a body (table-driven test…
descriptions.github:5684207074: What is wrong run.( Engine).Submit checks ActiveRunForLock and then calls CreateRun as two separate statements. The index on runs.lock key is not unique, so two submits that land between those calls both succeed. That can happen with two UI requests, or the CLI in one terminal and the UI in another. Two runs then hold one lock, which is exactly what ADR-0004 exists to prevent. What we want Make the check and the insert one atomic statement, so it also holds across processes: Report zero rows affected as the LockConflictError . The alternative is a partial unique index on lock key WHERE status IN (…) AND lock key != '' , which needs a migration. Where to look - src/internal/run/engine.go ( Submit ) - src/internal/store/runs.go ( CreateRun , ActiveRunForLock ) - src/internal/store/migrations/ if you take the index route Definition of done - [ ] A test submits the same lock key…
descriptions.github:5684206511: What is wrong labctl never installs a signal handler, so cmd.Context() is context.Background() and Ctrl-C kills the process with Go's default action. Scripts started through internal/toolchain run in their own process group ( Setpgid ), so the terminal's SIGINT does not reach them. They keep running with no parent, and their run stays running until the next engine start reconciles it. That breaks the promise in ADR-0003. Two smaller effects of the same gap: - labctl ui exits without calling Shutdown on the HTTP server. - scenario verify --watch sleeps with time.Sleep , which no context can interrupt. What we want - In cli.Execute , run the root command under signal.NotifyContext(ctx, os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM) via rootCmd.ExecuteContext . Everything already reads cmd.Context() , so cancellation flows to run.Engine and each process group gets its graceful SIGTERM. - labctl ui calls…
descriptions.github:5684205957: What is wrong Engine.Get returns the Scenario held in the engine's cache, but only after setting s.Active on it. Any two goroutines that call Get at the same time, or one that calls Get while a run reads the scenario, race on that field. - go test -race ./internal/service/scenario/ reports it on main in TestActivate ConflictsPerScenario , which fails most runs. - The race is also live in labctl ui , because its HTTP handlers call Get concurrently. What we want Stop writing to the cached value. Return a shallow copy with Active filled in, so every caller stays the same. (Dropping the field in favour of IsActive(name) is the alternative, but it touches every caller; take the copy approach first.) Where to look - src/internal/scenario/engine.go ( Get , isActive ) - src/internal/service/scenario/ for the failing test Definition of done - [ ] Get never mutates the cached scenario. - [ ] A…
descriptions.github:5684205515: What is wrong Engine.Down prints an uninstall error as a warning, carries on, removes the .active marker and returns success. On a lab whose API server was timing out, scenario down event-driven-arch and scenario down gitops-cicd both reported succeeded while every kubectl delete failed with TLS handshake timeout . Producers, consumers, the ArgoCD Applications, namespaces, ServiceMonitors and dashboard ConfigMaps were all left running. What we want 1. Down collects uninstall errors. When any component fails it keeps the marker, names the failed components, and returns an error telling the user…

descriptions.github:5684142179: Problem A: In Admin → Users → "Change pw", leaving the field empty and pressing Save sends the request. The server silently ignores an empty password ( if (password) ), but the UI closes the editor as if it had been saved. Problem B: If creating a user fails, the message is shown as Error: Username already taken — with the "Error:" prefix ( String(createMut.error) ). Other pages (Wrapped, Discover) strip the prefix. Where: web/src/pages/admin/UsersPage.tsx What to do: (A) disable Save while the password field is empty (or don't submit). (B) strip the prefix or use error.message . Acceptance criteria - [ ] Two new tests in UsersPage.test.tsx : Save is disabled / no request for an empty password; the error message is shown without the prefix.
descriptions.github:5684141991: A few actions swallow errors and show nothing, so the user presses a button and nothing seems to happen. Don't change the existing behaviour (optimistic revert etc.). descriptions.github:5683888258: Reproduction On current main , fetch the spec the server serves and look for $ref s that point at schemas it doesn't define: Expected Every $ref in /openapi.json resolves. Actual GET /v1/sessions/{session id}/stream declares its text/event-stream response as $ref: /components/schemas/ServerStreamEvent , but the live document never defines ServerStreamEvent . Only scripts/dump openapi.py adds it, when writing the committed openapi.json , so the checked-in file is fine and the served one isn't. Why it matters /docs and any client generator or validator pointed at a running server's /openapi.json hit an unresolved reference on the session stream, which is the main way clients follow a session. Proposed fix Register the ServerStreamEvent union (and its per-event variants) in the app's OpenAPI document, and have scripts/dump openapi.py reuse that instead of keeping its own copy. The…

descriptions.github:5683824411: Outcome pnpm run test only runs the repository's own test files and passes on a machine that has agent worktrees checked out under .claude/worktrees/ . Current behavior - vite.config.ts excludes defaultExclude and /.kimi/ , but not /.claude/ . - Vitest therefore collects every test file inside .claude/worktrees/ . With four worktrees present, a local run reports 396 failed | 135 passed test files, although all 785 tests of the main checkout pass. The worktree files fail at import ( TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'config') ) because they resolve against a different dependency tree. - CI is not affected because it has no worktrees, so the failure only shows up locally and hides real regressions. Expected behavior - Add /.claude/ to test.exclude in vite.config.ts . - A local pnpm run test with worktrees present reports only the 135 test files of the main checkout.

The caller never appears to use the callee, so the callee can be reported unreachable and the graph is missing the edge. packages/core/src/repowise/core/ingestion/queries/go.scm:50-70 Every call pattern in the file is rooted at call expression . descriptions.github:5683511344: Problem or use case There is no omni command that closes or deletes a session. The API supports it ( DELETE /v1/sessions/{id} ), and the web UI can archive. From a terminal, the closest is omni host stop-session . That stops the runner but leaves the session in the list. A script or a user cleaning up test or probe sessions must call the HTTP API by hand, with a bearer token. Proposed solution omni session close ... (archive) and omni session delete ... (with a confirm, or --yes ). Both should take --server and use the same auth as omni session export . Alternatives considered curl -X DELETE with a token from the server's auth flow. It works, but it is undiscoverable and makes users handle tokens themselves. Related: 4834 and 7498 (the agent-side sys session close gaps).

descriptions.github:5683459075: Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe. When using the MPU and deleting a FreeRTOS object, I am responsible for revoking access to the to-be-deleted object for each task which uses it. Describe the solution you'd like I'd like all FreeRTOS object deletion APIs to automatically clear any granted ACL permissions to the surviving tasks. Describe alternatives you've considered The current guidance here is to revoke ACL permissions before deleting the object, however this is annoying to manage. How many devices will this feature impact? Unknown What are your project timelines? Flexible Additional context The interplay between ACL and the object deletion APIs have been frustrating for at least 2 customers. If you have the same (or similar) feature request, please upvote this issue with thumbs up 👍 and use the comments section to provide answers to the questions above.

descriptions.github:5681673047: Summary Only SIGQUIT is handled. SIGTERM and SIGINT use the default action, so the process dies at once and leaves the pid file behind. nginx does a fast shutdown on TERM/INT: it closes connections and deletes the pid file. Repro pid logs/r.pid; , start, kill -TERM . - nginx: exits 0, pid file removed. - ruxen: killed by the signal (exit status 143), logs/r.pid left behind. nginx reference src/os/unix/ngx process.c:55-58 (terminate signal); src/os/unix/ngx process cycle.c:660 ( ngx delete pidfile ). Unlocks — Notes Same flag plumbing as SIGQUIT, with no drain. Where in ruxen src/main.rs --- Reproduced on 23a0c43 . Good first issue: small and self-contained. See CONTRIBUTING.md; comment here before starting so two people don't do the same work.
descriptions.github:5681672067: Summary All three directives are ignored, so Set-Cookie from the upstream is passed through unchanged. Repro The upstream sends Set-Cookie: a=b; domain= path=/old/; Secure . Config: proxy cookie domain example.com; proxy cookie path /old/ /new/; proxy cookie flags a httponly samesite=strict nosecure; . - nginx: domain=example.com; path=/new/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict , without Secure . - ruxen: unchanged. nginx reference ngx http proxy module.c:2699 (cookie rewrite), :4564 (flags). Unlocks proxy cookie.t (1–8) and proxy cookie flags.t (1–7, 9–10, 12–14). Both files then pass. Notes It is a response-header rewrite on the proxy path only; supports variables and regex ( / ). It can be split into three PRs, one per directive. Where in ruxen src/config/mod.rs --- Reproduced on 23a0c43 .
descriptions.github:5681671532: Summary proxy method is accepted and ignored, so the upstream always sees the client's method. Repro location /m { proxy method POST; proxy pass } with an upstream that echoes $request method , then curl /m . - nginx: upstream sees POST . - ruxen: upstream sees GET . nginx reference src/http/modules/ngx http proxy module.c:439 (directive), :1236 ( ngx http proxy create request ). Unlocks proxy method.t (2–4; the file then passes). Notes It is a complex value (variables allowed) and inherits from the parent. Render it into the request line in run location handler . Take it off IGNORED STMT in the same PR. Where in ruxen src/config/mod.rs --- Reproduced on 23a0c43 . Good first issue: small and self-contained. See CONTRIBUTING.md; comment here before starting so two people don't do the same work.
descriptions.github:5681671059: Summary types {} is swallowed and default type is ignored. MIME types come from a hardcoded 18-entry table that appends ; charset=utf-8 to text types, and unknown extensions get application/octet-stream . nginx uses the configured types map ( include mime.types in practice), falls back to default type (default text/plain ), and adds no charset unless charset is set. Repro Request /a.foo , /noext and /index.html . - nginx: text/x-foo , text/x-default , text/html . - ruxen: application/octet-stream , application/octet-stream , text/html; charset=utf-8 . nginx reference src/http/ngx http core module.c:311,319 (directives), :3660 (built-in default types), ngx http set content type . Unlocks — Notes Build a per-location HashMap at prepare time; the hot path does one lowercase-extension lookup, as now. Re-measure m3 and static 8k . Keeping the charset suffix would need charset support. Where…
descriptions.github:5681670291: Summary ssl protocols TLSv1 TLSv1.1 TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; is a hard error ( insecure version rejected: TLSv1 ). That exact line is in common distro default nginx.conf files, so unmodified configs don't load. rustls can't speak TLS 1.0/1.1 anyway. Repro http { ssl protocols TLSv1 TLSv1.1 TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; ... } , then ruxen -t . - nginx: ok. - ruxen: [emerg] bad value for ssl protocols (insecure version rejected): TLSv1 . nginx reference src/http/modules/ngx http ssl module.c ( ssl protocols bitmask). Unlocks ssl sni reneg.t gets past config load. Its renegotiation subtests then fail by design in rustls, so it won't fully pass. Notes Keep TLSv1.2/1.3 from the list and log [warn] TLSv1, TLSv1.1 are not supported and ignored . A list with only old versions should still be [emerg] . Where in ruxen src/config/mod.rs --- Reproduced on 23a0c43 . Good first issue: small and self-contained. See…
descriptions.github:5681669939: Summary include conf.d/ .conf; fails with open() "conf.d/ .conf" failed . nginx expands the glob, sorts the matches, and accepts a pattern that matches nothing. Repro location / { include conf.d/ .conf; return 200; } with conf.d/a.conf present, then ruxen -t . - nginx: syntax ok. - ruxen: [emerg] open() ".../conf.d/ .conf" failed , exit 1. nginx reference src/core/ngx conf file.c:821-870 ( ngx conf include , ngx open glob ). Unlocks — (very common in real configs, e.g. include /etc/nginx/conf.d/ .conf ) Notes Expand only when the path contains ? . Sort the matches. -T must dump every expanded file. --- Reproduced on 23a0c43 . Good first issue: small and self-contained. See [CONTRIBUTING.md; comment here before starting so two people don't do the same work.

descriptions.github:5681669368: Summary There are three separate reason-phrase tables, and any code they don't list becomes OK : return 413 sends HTTP/1.1 413 OK , and the same goes for 307/308/406/414/416/429/504. 503 says Service Unavailable , where nginx says Service Temporarily Unavailable . nginx sends NNN with an empty reason for codes it doesn't know (205, 418, 599). Repro location = /413 { return 413; } (likewise 307, 504, 418), then curl -si . - nginx: 413 Request Entity Too Large , 307 Temporary Redirect , 504 Gateway Time-out , 418 . - ruxen: 413 OK , 307 OK , 504 OK , 418 OK . - client max body size overflow also answers 413 OK . nginx reference src/http/ngx http header filter module.c:58+ ( ngx http status lines[] ). Unlocks — Notes One const table indexed like nginx's, used by all three call sites. For 418/599, nginx also sends no body and no Content-Type. Where in ruxen src/http.rs , src/file.rs…

When the window is too small, the device picker says "resize to at least 56 × 20", then keeps showing that message until a key is pressed. The compare device picker ( c ) polls every 250 ms and does follow a resize. Each render already reads the current terminal size. The drawing code already has tests with fixed sizes, so check this change by hand: shrink a…
descriptions.github:5681660786: What happens Both jobs set CI TIER and CI BUDGET MIN , and the header comment says every job declares a cost tier and budget. Nothing in this repository reads them. The only enforced limit is timeout-minutes: 15 on build ; changes has none. The matrix pins macos-14 but uses ubuntu-latest , which changes whenever GitHub updates that image. Where - .github/workflows/ci.yml:3-4 - .github/workflows/ci.yml:25-28 - .github/workflows/ci.yml:67-74 Suggested fix Either remove the variables and the comment, or make the budget real with timeout-minutes on each job. Pin Linux to a fixed image such as ubuntu-24.04 in both jobs. The CI run on the pull request is the test.
descriptions.github:5681660369: What happens environmentReader recognizes std.process.getEnvVarOwned and std.process.hasEnvVarConstant . Neither exists in Zig 0.16, so that branch can never match real code; only a test fixture uses it. Meanwhile, 0.16 readers such as Environ.containsUnempty and Environ.Map.getPtr are not recognized. Names starting with ZZZBENCH or XDG are still caught by the prefix rule. Where - tools/tidy.zig:268-284 - tools/tidy.zig:320-339 (the fixture) Suggested fix Remove the std.process branch. Add containsUnempty and getPtr to the recognized reader names. Change the fixture line to a 0.16 call and keep the expected count. To test, run zig build test -Dtest-filter="environment" .
descriptions.github:5681659886: Description servers/apache/tests/.gitignore is a deny-all whitelist: it starts with and then lists every tracked fixture with a ! line. A new fixture is therefore gitignored by default and has to be un-ignored by hand. A recent PR hit it: 538 (PR 552) added body-limit-large.html and body-limit-small.html for the new MesiMaxBodySize tests. Both were ignored until ! lines were added; without them the new tests 404 in CI. 542 (PR 557) needed no new fixture, but the same list is now 39 lines long and every PR that adds an HTML page has to remember it. The failure mode is silent and confusing: git status is clean, the file exists locally, the developer runs test.sh and sees it work, and CI gets a 404. It costs a full review round plus a CI cycle to notice. Where to start servers/apache/tests/.gitignore . Options, cheapest first: 1. Invert the file: allow the known-safe patterns instead of…

descriptions.github:5681659150: What happens writeFd loops until every byte is written, but it returns early, without an error, when write returns 0. The caller sees success while the rest of the frame was dropped. wire.zig treats the same case as an error. Where - tools/zzzbench/tty.zig:39-46 - tools/zzzbench/wire.zig:303-316 ( writeWireBytes returns error.ProbeGone when n == 0 ) Suggested fix Return an error when n == 0 instead of returning normally. A real file descriptor does not return 0 for a non-empty write, so move the loop into a function that takes the write call as a parameter, and test it with a stub that returns 0. tty.zig has no tests today, so register it in tools/zzzbench/tests.zig .
descriptions.github:5681659211: Description examples/php-ext-cache-memcached.php:27-28 tells the reader that php-ext's cache memcached servers validator enforces "the same restriction as the Apache MesiCacheMemcachedServers validator". The two do not match, in two independent ways: - ' (single quote). Apache rejected it only in 542 (PR 557, ). php-ext's parse host port - mesi is safe string ( php-ext/mesi.c:535 , :169 ) does not reject it, so a PHP user writing 'mc:11211' gets it accepted and the host never resolves - the example says otherwise. - DEL ( 0x7f ). php-ext's mesi is safe string rejects it; Apache's MesiCacheMemcachedServers validator checks only c < 0x20 and accepts it (tracked separately as 559). So the drift predates 542; 542 widened it by one byte. This matters because the same false-equivalence blocked 542's review on docs/features.md , where a "the PHP extension has the same rule" clause had been…

descriptions.github:5681658354: What happens statusWidth reserves room for the status chip using .len on string literals such as "✓ done" . The symbols ✓ , ✗ , ○ and ● are 3 bytes each but take 1 cell, so every chip is counted 2 cells too wide. The chip is then drawn 2 cells short of the right edge, and the sparkline loses those 2 cells. Keep the label strings in one place so statusWidth and writeStatus cannot disagree. To test, render writeStatus for each state into a fixed buffer and check that tui.cell.width(buffer) == statusWidth(p) . Then run zig build update-golden , read the snapshot diff, and…
descriptions.github:5681658012: What happens - Peer.canRunEngine has no callers. main.zig checks hello.has engine directly. - MmapReader has a bounds check, twelve read helpers, and skip . None of them are used. The only caller, model catalog.inspect , uses init , deinit and .data , and GGUF parsing happens in gguf metadata.zig with its own cursor. - model catalog.inspect takes a gpa and throws it away with = gpa; . Where - tools/zzzbench/peer.zig:66-69 - shared/mmap reader.zig:31-115 - tools/zzzbench/model catalog.zig:139-149 Suggested fix 1. Delete canRunEngine . 2. Cut MmapReader down to init , deinit and data , or replace it with a small map/unmap function. 3. Drop the gpa parameter and update the one call. Neither module is exported, so nothing outside the repository is affected. To test, run zig build check and zig build test . If a file is removed, tools/tidy.zig reports any import left pointing at it.

The check is c < 0x20 , so 0x7f passes. The sibling validators do…

descriptions.github:5681621264: Use case I am using the hive for FMA, dashboard at . It is on the release channel named "stable". I want to know when my hive will next be updated. descriptions.github:5681561743: Why The Appearance dialog draws clickable controls, but its keyboard handling currently only supports Escape. descriptions.github:5681551856: 赏金平台 / Platform GitHub 原始链接 / Source URL 漏洞描述 / Description [Bounty $1,000] FP32 ttnn.cumsum returns NaN after infinity or overflow 📝 Background ttnn.cumsum has a regression in its compensated FP32 accumulation path. After the running total becomes +inf or -inf—either because an input contains an infinity or because the sum overflows—subsequent output elements become NaN. This behavior diverges from PyTorch: Input: [1.0, inf, 1.0, 1.0] ttnn: [1.0, inf, nan, nan] torch: [1.0, inf, inf, inf] The regression was introduced by the compensated-summation change in 56811. The compensation calculation performs inf - inf, producing NaN; subsequent scan elements are then poisoned. The issue affects the default FP32 path. The existing disable compensated sum=True path avoids the failure but is deprecated and is not an acceptable long-term workaround. 🎯 What Success Looks Like The bounty is complete…

descriptions.github:5681232002: 🤖 This issue was found and written with AI (Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5). Problem --clear-session doesn't actually clear the session. In main.py the browser context is created first, and aenter loads storage state.json into it. Only after that does session.clear session() delete the file: The run still uses the old cookies, and aexit writes them back to disk. So the flag is a no-op. Fix - Delete the file before creating the context, e.g. by passing a fresh=True option to BrowserSession or by deleting it in main.py before the async with . - Alternatively, call context.clear cookies() like --form-login does. - Add a test asserting the context is created with storage state=None when --clear-session is given.

descriptions.github:5681087603: Summary codeprism scan . --diff validates the range with SAFE GIT REF RE , which allows a leading - . A value such as --stat , -p or --shortstat is therefore passed to git diff --name-only as an option, and the scan reports "No changed files" and exits 0. In a CI gate, a bad value passes silently instead of failing. (Git rejects branch names starting with - , so this is a hardening gap rather than an easy exploit, but the check exists specifically to keep git arguments safe.) Steps to reproduce Uses a throwaway git repository. Actual behaviour SAFE GIT REF RE = r"^[\w./ ^@{}:+\-]{1,200}$" ( codeprism/cli.py ) matches --stat , -p and --help . Expected behaviour A range starting with - is rejected with the existing "Invalid diff range" message and exit 1. Suggested fix - Require the first character not to be - , for example ^(?!-)[\w./ ^@{}:+\-]{1,200}$ . - Also pass --end-of-options (or…

descriptions.github:5680992241: GroqClient.SystemPrompt hard-codes English: The model handles many languages perfectly well. The only reason the review is English-only is that the prompt says so. What to build The flag should substitute the target language into the prompt and translate the section headings to match, so the output reads naturally rather than as translated English headings over a non-English body. Why it matters This project was built for the developer with no team to ask. That developer is not necessarily an English speaker, and a review you have to translate before you can act on it is a review you will skip. Notes - Default stays English, so nothing changes for existing users. - Accept ISO 639-1 codes ( pt , es , fr , de , ja ) and fall back to English with a warning on stderr for anything unrecognised. - Nothing parses the section names, so they are free to translate.
descriptions.github:5680986143: The CLI reviews local changes ( git diff , --staged , --diff ). It cannot review a pull request that is not checked out locally. What to build GitHub serves the raw diff for any PR at .diff , so this can be a plain HTTP GET followed by the existing review path — no API client, and no authentication needed for public repositories. Why it matters It turns the tool from "review what I am about to commit" into "review what someone sent me", which is the other half of reviewing alone: the maintainer triaging a drive-by contribution with nobody to ask for a second opinion. Notes - Private repositories need a token; treat that as a follow-up, not part of this. - Large PRs will hit the existing 60k-character truncation. That is fine, but the warning should name the PR that was truncated. - Parsing the URL belongs in CliOptions ; fetching belongs in its own small type next to GitDiff .

So a client cannot display "this will cost approximately X" before the user commits. The user sees only…

The arrow buttons next to it are labelled just "Move up" / "Move down" ( :143, :150 ), without the brain's name. Scenario VoiceOver reads every row's switch as "switch, on". A blind user can't tell which brain they're about to turn off or reorder. descriptions.github:5680942615: Problem Sources/MomoApp/Context/ContextMonitor.swift:29 declares notificationsReady = false . It is set only once, at launch, in prepareNotifications() ( :210-215 ). Both notify ( :222 ) and scheduleReminderNotifications ( :247 ) start with guard canNotify, notificationsReady else { return } . Scenario The user declines the first-launch notification prompt, then later enables Momo in System Settings → Notifications. Until Momo is relaunched, all of these are silently dropped: - Task reminders - Routine replies - "Needs your answer" prompts - Meeting-note offers - The morning greeting A routine waiting on a consent prompt hangs with no signal at all. Suggested fix - Check UNUserNotificationCenter.current().notificationSettings().authorizationStatus before posting, or re-check on NSApplication.didBecomeActiveNotification . - Consider listing Notifications in the Permissions pane.
descriptions.github:5680942128: Problem Sources/MomoApp/Support/KeychainStore.swift:25-39 : setKey first calls SecItemDelete , then return SecItemAdd(...) == errSecSuccess . The method is marked , and every caller ignores the result: - Settings/AI/APIKeySetupView.swift:148 (sets result = .valid right after) - Settings/BrainSettingsView.swift:282 - Settings/ConnectionsSettingsView.swift:125 Scenario The user replaces a working key. SecItemAdd fails (the keychain is locked or access is denied). By then the old key has already been deleted and the new one wasn't saved, yet the UI shows "valid / connected". The next chat fails with an authentication error, far from the real cause. Suggested fix - Update the item with SecItemUpdate , falling back to SecItemAdd , so the old key is never deleted first. - Check the result at each call site (or make setKey throw the OSStatus ) and show an error instead of .valid .
descriptions.github:5680936876: Problem Sources/MomoMCP/MCPClient.swift:56-70 : LineBuffer.append keeps appending data until it sees \n , with no size limit. Both ProcessTransport and UnixSocketTransport use it. The server side already caps its buffer at 16 MB ( MCPSocketServer.swift:191 ); the client side has no cap. descriptions.github:5680936294: Problem Sources/MomoApp/Context/MCPConnections.swift:66-77 starts the server process with ProcessTransport . descriptions.github:5680620805: conv can turn a GIF into an mp4 but not a webm, and webm is what a lot of sites want for short loops. GIF TO MP4 in crates/convkit-core/src/registry.rs is the template. Same idea, but encoded with VP9 the way VIDEO TO WEBM does it ( libvpx-vp9 , -crf with WEBM CRF , -b:v 0 ). GIFs have no audio, so leave out the opus flags. Keep Arg::VideoChain(&TRANSCODE CHAIN) so --fps and --resize still work, and register it next to the gif - mp4 line in insert media family . The "looping GIF becomes a single play" warning applies here too. One thing to check: GIFs can have transparent pixels, and VP9 webm can carry alpha ( -pix fmt yuva420p ). If that works, keep it. If not, add a warning saying transparency is lost. Done when conv in.gif out.webm works, the recipe snapshot has the new line, and the pair count at the top of the README is updated. CONTRIBUTING.md has the steps.

descriptions.github:5680591943: Description cli/mesi-cli.go never closes the HTTP response body. In URL mode the body is fetched at client.Do(req) ( cli/mesi-cli.go:306 ) and read with io.ReadAll(content.Body) ( cli/mesi-cli.go:317 ), but there is no defer content.Body.Close() anywhere, so the http.Response is dropped unread on every path that leaves the URL branch. Impact today is small but real: - the body is read to EOF on the success path, so the connection is handed back to the pool anyway and main returns immediately afterwards; - on every error branch os.Exit(1) is called, and os.Exit runs no deferred functions, so a defer content.Body.Close() placed at the top of the branch would not fire there either — the fds are only reclaimed when the process dies. So no leak is observable from the CLI as it is used today. The defect is the missing Close() itself: it is invisible only because the process is short-lived…

That guidance does not travel with a brief when someone copies only the generated Markdown into a coding assistant. Do not modify or interpret report instructions, execute commands, or add a hosted-model integration. Acceptance criteria - Use a synthetic failure containing an instruction-like sentence and show the complete proposed output. - State plainly that report contents are untrusted diagnostic data and require independent review. - Count the notice in the character budget, including the…

In pipelines that immediately parse the result, whitespace adds bytes without adding information. A compact serialization option could reduce artifact size while preserving all records and existing field semantics. It must not be confused with shortening failure content or imposing a total-output budget; those have different effects on what consumers receive. Scope Discuss an explicit JSON-only compact mode using standard-library serialization. Keep pretty-printed JSON as the default unless a separate compatibility decision is made. descriptions.github:5680542819: Why this is useful Markdown is useful for sharing briefs, but literal backslash escapes and code fences can be distracting when reading output in a terminal or plain-text log viewer. A dedicated text renderer could serve those users while keeping the same privacy and size guarantees. This should be a small alternative presentation layer, without terminal colors, network calls, or assumptions that the destination supports rich formatting. Scope Propose a plain-text layout for the existing Failure fields and agree whether it shares the Markdown budget option or has a separate clearly named limit. Acceptance criteria - Provide a concrete before/after example containing punctuation-heavy test names and a multiline traceback. - Preserve suite, class, source, kind, message, and details when budget allows. - Keep terminal-control sanitization, secret redaction, deterministic order, and…

Acceptance criteria - Define record types and ordering so consumers can identify metadata without guessing from field names. - Keep embedded newlines escaped within one physical line and preserve Unicode and sanitization. - Ensure invalid later input emits no partial success and atomic file…

A documented fingerprint could simplify matching, but careless hashing can create misleading stability or disclose information through guessing attacks. Scope Start with a design for an optional fingerprint derived from agreed sanitized identity fields, separate from parser deduplication and without changing its current behavior. Acceptance criteria - Specify normalization, included fields, algorithm, version tag, and handling of source paths. - Explain whether changing a traceback or excerpt budget should change the identifier, with concrete examples. - Do not hash raw secrets or present…

A consumer that wants to show a truncated badge for one failure must inspect that text, which could also occur literally in a report. Explicit per-field metadata would let integrations distinguish original content from transformation information without parsing an English sentence. Scope Design a backward-compatible extension or new schema version that represents original sanitized length, retained length, and truncation status for message and details. Acceptance criteria - Specify lengths after redaction and explain whether notice characters are included in each count. - Cover untouched, shortened, empty, and literal-notice content without relying on substring detection. - Keep original secret lengths and matched values out…

A schema describing the existing contract would make integrations easier to build and review. Scope Add a checked-in JSON Schema for the version 1 envelope and failure records, plus a short pointer from the JSON documentation. Keep runtime dependencies unchanged. Acceptance criteria - Specify required properties, data types, schema version, and the actual supported kind values. - Define whether unknown fields are accepted, explaining the compatibility tradeoff rather than assuming one. - Include representative empty and non-empty valid examples and an…
descriptions.github:5680539876: Why this is useful Many reports put the same short exception text in the message attribute and at the start of the detail body. The current renderer shows both, which can spend a meaningful share of a small context budget on repeated information. A conservative presentation rule could improve readability, but fuzzy similarity or broad prefix deletion might remove an important distinction in an assertion. Scope Evaluate an opt-in Markdown-only rule for exact duplicated message lines after sanitization. Preserve the original structured fields and avoid changing parser deduplication. Acceptance criteria - Provide synthetic examples for an exact first-line duplicate, a near match, and a genuinely repeated diagnostic line. - Define treatment of whitespace and omission notices; do not accidentally compare truncated text as full evidence. - Keep differing messages and details intact and…
descriptions.github:5680539332: Why this is useful The Markdown header currently reports one total for all unique failure records. With many suites, a reader must scan the individual blocks to understand where failures cluster. A small per-suite summary could help prioritize investigation, particularly when the output budget omits later details. It must clearly summarize extracted unique records rather than claiming to reproduce original runner counters or the total number of executed tests. Scope Discuss an optional summary grouped by the suite identity already available in Failure. Do not change parsing, suite ancestry, deduplication, or failure selection. Acceptance criteria - Include a synthetic report with repeated suite names across reports and define the grouping key explicitly. - Ensure totals agree with the complete extracted failure set, including records whose details are omitted. - Bound summary size and…
descriptions.github:5680538872: Why this is useful The renderer deliberately keeps an ordered prefix of complete failure blocks. If the first block is too large, a brief may contain only the total and an omission notice even when later failures have useful short descriptions. Some workflows would benefit from seeing every selected test identity before allocating remaining space to details. This would be an alternative presentation strategy, not a parser-order change or a new failure filter. Scope Prototype an opt-in summary-first renderer that budgets concise identities before adding detailed blocks. Keep the current ordered-prefix strategy available. descriptions.github:5680538142: Why this is useful Character slicing uses Python code points, which is the documented budget unit, but a visible character can contain several code points. An excerpt boundary can separate an accent from its letter or split a joined emoji in a test message. This is mainly a readability issue and does not justify changing the tool into a tokenizer or silently adopting a new budget unit. Scope Evaluate conservative display-boundary adjustments for combining marks and joined sequences while keeping the current Unicode-character budget contract explicit. Discuss dependency costs before choosing an algorithm. Acceptance criteria - Use small synthetic cases with combining accents, variation selectors, and joined emoji around both excerpt boundaries. - Never exceed the agreed retained-content limit after adjusting a boundary; explain any under-filled budget. - Keep ordinary ASCII excerpt…
descriptions.github:5680537467: Why this is useful The existing excerpt function keeps a character-counted prefix and suffix, preserving the final exception in long traces. It can nevertheless cut through the middle of a filename, source line, or exception sentence. A line-aware option could make the retained evidence easier to read while retaining the bounded output goal. Exact character slicing remains a reasonable default and is covered by existing tests. Scope Design an optional excerpt strategy that favors complete lines near the head and tail, with a defined fallback for one extremely long line. descriptions.github:5680536950: Why this is useful The CLI excerpts failure messages and details, but suite, class, test name, and source fields can still be very long. Because Markdown currently includes only complete failure blocks, a large parameterized test name can consume the budget and prevent even a short assertion from appearing. Scope Define per-field display limits for Markdown metadata with visible omission markers. Preserve complete structured values in JSON unless a separately agreed policy says otherwise. Acceptance criteria - Use a synthetic parameterized test name and long class/source fields that currently hide a useful short failure. - Keep secret removal before display clipping and avoid cutting generated redaction markers. - Count escaping and…
descriptions.github:5680536433: Why this is useful Sanitization occurs before excerpt , which correctly avoids exposing the raw matched value. However, the excerpt slices arbitrary character positions. A short detail budget applied to TOKEN=[REDACTED] can retain only pieces of the replacement marker around the omission notice. That does not reveal the original secret, but it makes the resulting text look corrupted and obscures whether content was hidden for privacy or shortened for length. These marks can affect how mixed-direction failure text appears, but they also have legitimate uses in Arabic and Hebrew text. Expanding deletion without examples would trade one readability problem for another. Scope Create a focused design for these three directional marks: preserve, remove, or visibly annotate them under a documented policy. Do not strip all non-ASCII text. Acceptance criteria - Use synthetic mixed-direction test names and traces, including legitimate Arabic or Hebrew text. - Show the visual or copied-text problem motivating any change and specify default versus opt-in behavior. - Preserve ordinary Unicode content and all existing terminal-control and newline…
descriptions.github:5680535390: Why this is useful A reader currently sees replacement markers but cannot distinguish how many recognized matches were removed, or which broad rule families were involved. Optional summary counts could make it easier to review an output transformation and detect unexpected over-redaction. Such counts must not be presented as proof that the brief is safe: zero matches only means that no supported pattern matched the available fields. descriptions.github:5680534881: Why this is useful Failure traces and report paths can reveal a developer username through paths such as /home/demo-person/project/test.py or C:\Users\DemoPerson\project\test.py . These are not credentials and are intentionally outside the current generic secret patterns. Some users still need to remove that personal context before sharing a brief, while keeping relative project paths useful for debugging. This is separate from normalizing report source paths. Scope Design an explicit privacy option that masks configured home-directory prefixes in every visible failure field, without discovering arbitrary personal files or rewriting paths by default. Acceptance criteria - Cover synthetic POSIX and Windows prefixes, separators, case policy, and paths containing spaces. - Use path-boundary-aware replacement so a short prefix cannot corrupt unrelated filenames or prose. - Preserve enough…

The current redactor operates on the displayed text; it is not an arbitrary decoder. Recursively decoding every field would risk changing useful evidence and creating unpredictable runtime costs. Harmless diagnostics such as token count=17 or secret length=12 are therefore candidates for masking even when the numbers explain the failing assertion. Relaxing this behavior blindly could expose real credentials, so the useful contribution is a small policy change supported by both sensitive and harmless synthetic examples. Scope Discuss a conservative key-boundary or narrow exception policy. Target diagnostic counters rather than introducing a general disable-redaction switch. Acceptance criteria - Provide before/after examples showing the lost debugging information and the intended supported exception. - Include credential names with prefixes, suffixes, hyphens, quotes, and varied case as negative controls. - Keep genuine credential assignments masked and…

Users currently cannot supply exact values they already know should disappear. An explicitly selected local literal list could complement the heuristics without adding a regex language or sending report content to another service. This should remain optional because treating broad strings as secrets can destroy useful diagnostic context. Scope Design a small literal-redaction input contract, including encoding, maximum file size, minimum entry length, ordering, and error behavior. Acceptance criteria - Construct fake marker names and payloads at runtime; never commit a real or usable private key. - Cover RSA, EC, encrypted, and generic private-key labels within the agreed supported set. - Keep public certificates and ordinary prose unchanged unless an explicitly documented rule applies. - Bound…
descriptions.github:5680532397: Why this is useful The current redactor handles bearer credentials and key-like assignments, but a failure containing Authorization: Basic DEMO VALUE or Cookie: session=demo-value; theme=dark has different structure. HTTP debugging output can appear inside failure details even though captured stdout is excluded. A grouped header policy would be easier to review and maintain than unrelated expressions for individual authentication providers. Acceptance criteria - Add synthetic cases for first, middle, repeated, blank, and percent-encoded sensitive query parameters. - Preserve harmless parameters, delimiters, and fragments exactly where the chosen contract permits. - Keep replacement idempotent and cover both standalone URLs and…
descriptions.github:5680531426: Why this would help Reports may be consumed while another process is still writing them. descriptions.github:5680523418: Feature Factory Simulation & Abstraction What to Solve? Binary Factorium must run on extremely limited hardware ( ), and thus cannot naively use a tiled simulation or the conventional model. The constrains together make it hard to solve easily. What should the simulator essentially contain or do ideally? It should: - Update O(1) when nothing changes - Update O(n) or O(log(n)) when changes happen (with n = parts to update ) - Not hang when numerous updates happen in a short period of time (also in long periods ideally) - Consume a fixed amount of RAM at any point. - Possibly be asynchronous. - Be Binary-Spectacular ;) I am not an expert in this field ;-; (\ unlike what most factory games with large/infinite world target, Binary Factorium's primary targets are the Fri3d Badges)

descriptions.github:5680482893: Why this matters src/core/detectors/similarity.ts exports sanitize , which every detector depends on before comparing text. Splitting a grapheme cluster in half can make two identical emoji sequences look different, or make a genuinely repeating sequence look distinct. Risky inputs that currently have no fixture coverage: - ZWJ sequences — 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦, 👩‍💻 (variation selector U+FE0F plus U+200D zero-width joiners) - Flag sequences — 🇯🇵 is two regional indicator code points, not one - Combining marks — e + U+0301 versus é as a single code point - RTL text — Arabic or Hebrew inside an otherwise LTR transcript - Emoji with skin-tone modifiers — 👍🏽 is a base plus a modifier If sanitize is not grapheme-aware, that is a real correctness bug in the comparison layer, not just missing tests. What to do 1. Write a short test in tests/ asserting that sanitize returns the same string for "e\u0301" and…

descriptions.github:5680391574: Summary shell.RunCmd unconditionally prepends /opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin to the PATH of every shell command it runs: This is macOS-specific and means Stitch silently assumes Homebrew. On Linux (or non-Homebrew macOS setups) the prepended paths don't exist and the code is just dead weight. It also makes it harder to run Stitch in CI or Docker containers. Task Make the PATH augmentation runtime-aware: 1. Detect the current OS using runtime.GOOS . 2. Only prepend the Homebrew paths when GOOS == "darwin" . 3. Relevant files - backend/internal/shell/shell.go — the entire change lives in the RunCmd function ( 60 lines total). descriptions.github:5679932145: The cheapest entry left in the ratchet. Array.prototype.sort() sorts in place , so it mutates the array it was given; toSorted() returns a new one. Why this one is worth doing properly rather than mechanically Two of the three production call sites are in data-table.component.ts , which sorts rows it was handed through an input() . Sorting those in place mutates the caller's array — a signal's value, in most cases — which is how a table can reorder data a parent component still believes it owns, without the parent's signal ever being set. Swapping to toSorted() is the fix, but each site is worth a glance to see whether anything downstream was relying on the mutation. Note toSorted() needs a reasonably current runtime target; it is available in the browsers this project targets and in the Node used for specs. Acceptance - unicorn/no-array-sort is gone from eslint-suppressions.json after…
descriptions.github:5679931860: One of the smaller ratchet entries, and an unusual one: every violation is in a spec file. Production code already goes through the STORAGE adapter; it is the tests that reach localStorage directly. Why it matters more than the count suggests no-restricted-globals exists because Web Storage is a trust boundary ( security.md §4) reached through a global rather than an import, and STORAGE KEYS is meant to be the reviewable inventory of what this origin persists. A spec that writes localStorage directly is also a spec that can pass while the adapter is bypassed — and it leaves state behind for whatever test runs next, since the key never goes through the inventory. What to do Use the fake storage adapter from src/app/testing/adapters ( provideFakeAdapters() ) instead of touching localStorage , and assert against it. Declare any key the test needs in core/adapters/storage/storage-keys.ts if…

A misspelt key - netwrokPolicy: , or connector: for connectors: - is silently ignored. Helm renders the default, the install succeeds, and the setting the operator believes is on is off. descriptions.github:5678907905: 📝 Background ttnn.cumsum has a regression in its compensated FP32 accumulation path. After the running total becomes +inf or -inf—either because an input contains an infinity or because the sum overflows—subsequent output elements become NaN. This behavior diverges from PyTorch: Input: [1.0, inf, 1.0, 1.0] ttnn: [1.0, inf, nan, nan] torch: [1.0, inf, inf, inf] The regression was introduced by the compensated-summation change in 56811. The compensation calculation performs inf - inf, producing NaN; subsequent scan elements are then poisoned. The issue affects the default FP32 path. The existing disable compensated sum=True path avoids the failure but is deprecated and is not an acceptable long-term workaround. 🎯 What Success Looks Like The bounty is complete when all of the following are satisfied: - FP32 ttnn.cumsum preserves IEEE/PyTorch behavior after +inf . - FP32 ttnn.cumsum…

descriptions.github:5677602459: cmd dmesg is a stub. Kernel logs go to serial (and the boot framebuffer early on) but there is no buffer userspace can read back, or if there is one it is not wired to a syscall. First step is checking what DEBUG in src/kernel/debug.h actually emits and whether a ring buffer exists. If not, add a small one behind the existing log path, then an extended syscall that snapshots it out under a lock, then make dmesg print it. Worth deciding what release builds do since most logging is debug only.
descriptions.github:5677600372: cmd lspci in src/usr/shell/shell cmds.cpp prints a stub line. PCI enumeration happens at boot in src/drivers/bus/pci/ but userspace never sees the device list. Needs a new extended syscall (297 or wherever the numbering is by then) that fills an array of small descriptors (bus, slot, function, vendor id, device id, class code) and returns the total count, same shape as SYS INPUT ENUM DEVICES. Then the builtin just prints the table. include/uapi/input.h plus the input enum case in src/kernel/core/syscall.cpp are the reference for the uapi side.
descriptions.github:5677599797: There is no netstat. The TCP and UDP tables live in src/net/tcp.cpp and src/net/udp.cpp but nothing exports counts to userspace (sockets in use, per state, rx/tx bytes). Simplest version is a small extended syscall filling a struct with tcp and udp socket counts per state, next free number is 297. sys net status in src/net/net.cpp is the pattern to copy, and the input enum devices case in src/kernel/core/syscall.cpp shows the array-plus-count shape. Then a netstat builtin in src/usr/shell/shell cmds.cpp that prints it. The socket tables are plain arrays so ktesting the counters is easy.
descriptions.github:5677599522: Every UDP socket has one 1500 byte receive slot with overwrite semantics (src/net/udp.cpp). If two datagrams land before the app calls recvfrom the first one is gone, and nothing reports it either. Turning the slot into a small ring, 4 entries or so, would fix the common case. The receive handoff runs inside net poll() under the table spinlock so the write path has to stay cheap, a memcpy into a preallocated ring is fine. Some way to see overflow would be good too, a debug warn or a dropped counter.
descriptions.github:5677599224: Every resolve goes out on the wire even when we just resolved the same name. dns resolve() in src/net/dns.cpp already retries three times with fresh transaction ids, there is just no cache anywhere. A ktest for expiry and eviction can go next to the dns tests in src/net/dns tests.cpp.

descriptions.github:5677007869: What happens Two fixtures in SecretDetectionTests.swift expect a signed URL to be classified as a secret, but their signature values are too short or too regular for the detector's generated-value rules, so the test fails while real signed URLs are masked correctly. - The S3 fixture's signature is 16 hex characters of a repeated pair; the hex rule needs 32 ( hexTokenLength , SecretShapes.swift:116 ) and the entropy rule needs at least 3.8 bits ( entropyFloor , :122 ). - The Azure fixture's sig decodes to 13 characters and falls under the same entropy floor. Measured with a standalone build of the detector: a realistic S3 SigV4 URL (64 hex signature), a GCS V4 URL (512 hex), an Azure SAS (44-character base64), a CloudFront URL, a 32-character ?token= and a JWT in an access token fragment all return .secret ; only these two fixtures return .link . descriptions.github:5676996549: Automated canary report (issue 8) Daily board-health scan ran at 2026-10-02T11:52:48.110Z and these boards returned 0 jobs : - seek Likely causes 1. The board changed its JSON response shape (each of LinkedIn guest, SEEK chalice-search, Greenhouse boards-API has done this at least once in the last 2 years). 2. The board is rate-limiting our IP (a common pattern - they return empty rather than 429). 3. The pre-existing "treat an empty 200 as suspicious" fix in scrape companies ( 14) means 0-job output is the canonical fall-through; investigate first before assuming configuration drift. Triage steps - Open ./target/release/atsassin scan --role engineer --boards --limit 5 locally and check the raw HTTP response. - If shape drift, file a fix immediately; if rate-limit, add --limit regression tests against a synthetic mock.

PromptDrift needs bounded, safe retry logic for transient errors, coupled with a maximum total request budget to prevent runaway API spend or infinite loops. descriptions.github:5676783179: Description Follow-up from 64 / PR 255 (review finding). src/BinaryDownloader.php ( download() , the curl setopt array() call): the return value is ignored. If cURL rejects one option, the remaining ones are skipped silently, so the HTTPS-only and redirect limits could be missing without any error. descriptions.github:5676728882: Why Some searches expand a tree of decisions one ply at a time: a game, a plan, a sequence of tool calls. The full tree does not fit, and there is no stored graph. Monte Carlo tree search keeps the branches it has tried, picks the next one with an upper confidence bound, and backs a score up the path. 133 covers finding a path through a successor function. This issue is the tree of sampled decisions on top of that idea. Proposed API In a new package search : Options: - WithIterations(n int) , default 100. - WithExploration(c float64) , default math.Sqrt2 . This is the UCB1 constant. - WithRand(r rand.Rand) . When nil, each rollout picks a uniform legal action with crypto/rand . A non-nil source makes the search reproducible. Behavior - A nil actions , next , or score returns an error. - WithIterations below 1 returns an error. - Selection walks from the root by UCB1 until it reaches a…
descriptions.github:5676728489: Why Nearest-neighbor search for retrieval keeps a stack of graphs. The top layer is sparse. The bottom layer contains every point. A search starts at the top, greedily walks to a closer neighbor, then drops a layer. That is the HNSW search. The points stay in the caller's table. The graph stores ids, because a vector is not a comparable label in any useful way. This issue is the layered graph and the greedy search. It is not a database. There is no index file, no metadata filter, and no delete. Proposed API A new package nn : Behavior - distance must be zero or positive. A negative distance returns an error at search or insert time. - m and efConstruction below 1 return an error from New . A nil distance returns an error. - k or ef below 1 returns an error from Search . - Insert of an id that is already present does nothing and returns nil. - The neighbor sets are chosen by the HNSW…
descriptions.github:5676728256: Why Some DAGs accept a vertex only after several successful samples, and only after its parents are accepted. Avalanche counts confidence that way. The sample itself is a network call. The library can own the counter and the parent rule. The caller owns the query. Proposed API In dag : Behavior - Directed acyclic graphs only. Otherwise gograph.ErrNotDirected or gograph.ErrDAGHasCycle . - sample , beta , or rounds below 1 returns an error. A nil query returns an error. - Parents are incoming neighbors. - A vertex with no parents may be accepted on its own run of successes. - A failed query resets that vertex's consecutive count to 0. It does not reset other vertices. - The result is in GetAllVertices order, and contains only accepted vertices. - Returned vertices are the graph's own pointers. - The function does not open a connection, pick peers, or sign anything. query is the whole…
descriptions.github:5676728025: Why A block DAG is not a chain. One way to order it is to paint a well-connected subset blue and leave the rest red. A set is a k-cluster when every member has at most k other members that it cannot reach and that cannot reach it. The largest such set is expensive to find. The greedy coloring used by GHOSTDAG walks in topological order and adds a vertex to the blue set when the blue anticone is still within k. This is that coloring. It is not a node, and it does not choose a block for a peer to mine on. HeaviestBranch is the walk on a tree. This is the coloring on a DAG. Proposed API In dag : Behavior - Directed acyclic graphs only. Otherwise gograph.ErrNotDirected or gograph.ErrDAGHasCycle . - k below 0 returns dag.ErrInvalidK . - Two vertices are incomparable when neither can reach the other. - The walk order is the stable topological order, the same one TopologySort returns. - A…
descriptions.github:5676727781: Why Some DAGs decide that event A has seen event B only when the paths between them cover a supermajority of authors. Hashgraph calls this strongly seeing. The predicate is ancestor counting. Virtual voting and witness election stay with the caller. Proposed API In dag : Behavior - Directed graphs only. Otherwise gograph.ErrNotDirected . - members below 1 returns an error. A nil author returns an error. - Missing from or to: gograph.ErrVertexDoesNotExist . - Seeing is reachability along directed edges, including a vertex seeing itself. - The threshold is strictly greater than 2 members/3 . For 4 members the threshold is more than 8/3, so 3 authors. The test should use that case. - Authors are compared with == . The function does not check that every author id is one of a fixed set. An author outside the expected set still counts as one distinct author, which can only make the count…
descriptions.github:5676727518: Why Fork choice on a tree of blocks walks from the root and, at each block, follows the child whose subtree carries the most weight. GHOST and LMD-GHOST are that walk. The weight is whatever the caller counts: work, stake, or the latest vote of each validator. The library does not know which. Proposed API In dag : Behavior - Directed graphs only. Otherwise gograph.ErrNotDirected . - A vertex with two incoming edges, or a vertex not reachable from root, returns dag.ErrNotTree . - A cycle returns gograph.ErrDAGHasCycle . - Subtree weight is the vertex's own weight plus the subtree weights of its children. A vertex is not counted twice. - Ties break by GetAllVertices order of the children. - The returned path starts at root and ends at a leaf. Vertices are the graph's own pointers. - Negative weights are allowed. They only change which child wins. - Missing root…
descriptions.github:5676727251: Why Max flow ( 193) asks how much can move. Some networks also have a price on each edge. Splitting a payment across channels is the usual case: send a given amount, stay inside each edge's capacity, and pay the least fee. Proposed API In flow , beside MaxFlow : Successive shortest paths with potentials. Costs may be negative. A negative cycle in the residual graph returns flow.ErrNegativeCycle . Behavior - amount below 0 returns an error. amount of 0 returns a shipment of value 0 and cost 0. - A negative capacity returns flow.ErrNegativeCapacity . - Missing source or sink: gograph.ErrVertexDoesNotExist . - Directed edges carry flow in their direction. An undirected edge shares its capacity across the two directions, and that capacity is not doubled. - For every vertex other than source and sink, flow in equals flow out. - Flow on an edge stays inside its capacity. - Among shipments of…
descriptions.github:5676726980: Why Clustering merges labels into groups as pairs arrive: two addresses that shared an input, two records that are the same entity. Building a graph first is an extra copy. Disjoint sets answer "are these the same group" in nearly constant time. Proposed API A new package unionfind : Union by rank and path compression. Behavior - Connected on a label that was never seen is false. - Union of a label with itself adds it and leaves it in a group of one. - Representatives are deterministic for a given sequence of calls. - Groups does not return a representative that the caller has to interpret. It returns the members. - The package does not know about graphs. A caller with a graph passes labels. Tests - Five unions that form two groups. Connected matches. Groups matches, in insertion order. - Path compression does not change Connected results. - Find on an unknown label returns false…
descriptions.github:5676726745: Why Some DAGs are ordered by a score that includes the ancestors, not by the vertex alone. A transaction pool ranks a transaction by the total fee of itself and everything that must come before it, divided by the total size of that same set. StableTopologySort can compare vertices, and it cannot see that sum. Proposed API In dag : Behavior - Directed acyclic graphs only. Otherwise gograph.ErrNotDirected or gograph.ErrDAGHasCycle . - The set for a vertex is itself plus every vertex that can reach it. - The key is the sum of num over that set, divided by the sum of den over that set. - A denominator sum of 0 returns dag.ErrZeroDenominator . - Ties break by GetAllVertices order. - Returned vertices are the graph's own pointers, one per vertex in the graph. - Empty graph: nil, nil. - This is a ranking, not a topological order. A later vertex can rank ahead of an ancestor. Callers who need a…
descriptions.github:5676726508: Why Callers often need the best few items, not a full ordering. A mempool keeps the highest-paying transactions. A ranking keeps the top vertices by score. Retrieval keeps the nearest matches. A full sort does more work than that, and it allocates a second copy of the whole list. Proposed API In util : Behavior - k below 0 returns util.ErrInvalidK . k of 0 returns an empty slice and a nil error. - A nil better returns an error. - A nil or empty items returns an empty slice. - The result is a new slice. items is left as it was. - Equal items keep their original order. - Running time is linear in the length of items times log of k , using a heap of size k . The doc comment says so. A caller who wants a nucleus-style prefix computes it from this ordered prefix. The function does not grow a sampling API. Tests - Ten integers, k of 3, the three largest in order. - Ties: two equal best items…
descriptions.github:5676726283: Why AStar ( 185) keeps every unsettled vertex in a heap. When the frontier is large, the memory is the problem. Iterative deepening A repeats a depth-first search with a rising limit on the estimated total cost, and stores only the current path. Planners use it when the graph of states does not fit in memory. Proposed API In path , with the same cost and heuristic contract as AStar : Behavior - Costs must be zero or positive. A negative cost returns path.ErrNegativeWeight . - The search raises the limit to the smallest f-value that was beyond the previous limit. - It returns a cheapest path when the heuristic is admissible. The doc comment says so. It does not check the heuristic. - Missing vertices, an unreachable goal, and start equal to goal follow AStar . - Ties break by vertex and edge order. - The doc comment says AStar is the better choice when the frontier fits in memory…
descriptions.github:5676725921: Why On a graph that branches widely, keeping every partial path is too expensive. Beam search keeps a fixed number of them and drops the rest. Decoders use it to keep a few partial sequences. The same bound keeps a path search inside a memory limit. The result can miss the cheapest path. That is the trade. Proposed API In path : Behavior - width below 1 returns path.ErrInvalidWidth . - Partial paths are simple. A vertex is not repeated on one path. - At each step the search keeps the width partial paths with the best score. Ties break by vertex order. - If the goal is never among the kept paths, path.ErrUnreachable . - Missing start or goal: gograph.ErrVertexDoesNotExist . - start equals goal: a one-vertex path and cost 0, for any positive width. - Returned vertices are the graph's own pointers. - The same graph, width, and score give the same path on every run. - The doc comment says a…
descriptions.github:5676725632: Why A route from one vertex to one other vertex does not need a distance for every vertex. Searching forward from the start and backward from the goal meets in the middle and settles fewer vertices on a large graph. Payment-channel routing and road routing both do this. Proposed API In path , beside AStar ( 185): Behavior - Directed graphs: the backward search walks incoming edges. Undirected graphs: either direction. - Missing start or goal: gograph.ErrVertexDoesNotExist . - Unreachable: path.ErrUnreachable . - start equals goal: a one-vertex path and cost 0. - A negative cost: path.ErrNegativeWeight . - The path vertices are the graph's own pointers, start first and goal last. - Ties break by the order vertices and edges were added. - The two searches stop once the cheapest meeting point is settled. They do not scan the whole graph when the goal is close. Tests - A path graph where…

descriptions.github:5673427734: Current behavior 🐛 BorderVisual (Skia) replaces its RectangleClip objects whenever the border or corner radius geometry changes, but never disposes the old ones. In UpdatePathsAndCornerClip() , the old childClipCausedByCornerRadius and backgroundClip are just set to null and new clips are created (L203-L212, L330-L346). Since 24230, RectangleClip caches one geometry (a native SKPath ) and only releases it in DisposeInternal() (RectangleClip.skia.cs L42). descriptions.github:5672955594: Why webhook() and buildEvent() return payload: Record . A handler written in TypeScript has to describe the shape of charge.success , refund.processed and the rest for itself, and a test that reads a field from a fixture needs a cast. The templates in src/providers/ already hold the shapes. Proposed Export a type per event, taken from the templates, and have webhook("paystack", "charge.success") return a payload of that type. A handler can then import the same types it is tested with. Open questions: whether to derive the types from the templates with ReturnType or write them out, and how to mark fields the provider sometimes leaves out. Found while building the shop use case on paylocal 0.1.0.
